It raises a whole series of new problems","explanation":"This is distinctive near-verbatim reuse of C12's objection to an improvised conference procedure."},{"child_excerpt":"the Charter of the United Nations authorizes members of government, and that of course includes Heads of Government and Foreign Ministers, to represent a member nation at the Security Council","parent_excerpt":"under the Charter, members of government, including Heads of Government and foreign Ministers, may represent a member nation at the Security Council","explanation":"The same specific Charter-based mechanism is reproduced with only minor rewording."},{"child_excerpt":"if such a meeting were generally desired, the United States would join in following that orderly procedure","parent_excerpt":"If such a meeting were generally desired, the United States would join in following that orderly procedure.","explanation":"The operative commitment is repeated essentially verbatim."},{"child_excerpt":"World War II was brought about by a series of acts of direct and indirect aggression against small nations","parent_excerpt":"We do not want to see a repetition of the progressive destruction of the independence of small nations which occurred during the 1930's and which led to the Second World War.","explanation":"The child extends C12's historical argument connecting aggression against small nations to World War II."}]}
